content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes in the history (e.g., after 70+ values), often overshooting by 2–5 points.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: tends to forecast lower prices after recent high values, but fails to capture the true momentum or persistence.
- Forecast lags the true trend by 1–3 days, particularly in upward movements — model reacts too slowly to new data.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility, especially in the last 5–7 days of the forecast, leading to erratic corrections.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price increases during periods of high demand or policy tightening (e.g., after 72+ in history).
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating the true range of price swings, especially in the final 10 days of the forecast.
